user.title: Set up Nimbus
user.description: This creates the Nimbus hub. Before adding loads, use the hub's own "Configure" to set your temperature sensors and tuning defaults once -- then add each load you want forecast (HWS, EV charger, pool, individual circuit breakers -- as many as you like) from the hub's device page, one at a time, without repeating this setup.

abort.already_configured: Nimbus is already set up -- add loads from its device page instead of adding it again.

menu_options.forecaster: Forecaster settings (shared sensors + tuning for every load/signal)
menu_options.solver_battery: Solver settings (your real battery/grid/solar setup, for dispatch planning)

forecaster.title: Nimbus settings (shared by every load/signal)
forecaster.description: These apply to every load or power signal you add -- set once here rather than re-entering them each time.

data.temperature_forecast_sensor: Temperature forecast sensor (optional, used for future predictions)
data.humidity_sensor: Humidity sensor (optional, improves accuracy for weather-sensitive loads)
data.curtailment_sensor: Curtailment switch (optional, for a load run only to soak up otherwise-curtailed solar)
data.battery_sensor: Battery power sensor (optional, real measured value -- never an optimizer's own plan/forecast)
data.grid_sensor: Grid power sensor (optional, real measured value -- never an optimizer's own plan/forecast)
data.solar_sensor: Solar power sensor (optional, real measured value -- never an optimizer's own plan/forecast)
data.train_days: Days of history to train on

solver_battery.title: Solver: Battery (1 of 6)
solver_battery.description: Your battery's own real, physical specs -- from the datasheet or your inverter/BMS's own app, not a guess. This is the ONE aggregate battery the Solver plans for: if you have more than one physical pack, add their capacities together and use a blended max power/efficiency -- your own inverter/BMS already handles how load is actually shared between packs internally, the Solver only needs to know the system's overall envelope.

data.solver_battery_capacity_kwh: Usable battery capacity (kWh) -- the real, nameplate usable capacity, not what a fresh cell rating claims
data.solver_battery_soh_percent: State of Health (%, optional) -- if your battery/BMS reports a real SoH, use it to shrink usable capacity as the pack ages; leave at 100% if you don't track this
data.solver_battery_soc_sensor: Battery State of Charge sensor (%) -- the live sensor your system already reports, e.g. from your inverter's own integration
data.solver_battery_min_soc_percent: Minimum SoC to protect (%, optional) -- the floor the Solver should never plan to discharge below (battery longevity / your own reserve preference)
data.solver_battery_max_soc_percent: Maximum SoC to charge to (%, optional) -- normally 100%, lower this if your own BMS caps charging below full for longevity

solver_power.title: Solver: Power & Efficiency (2 of 6)
solver_power.description: The real power limits and losses of your battery + inverter system together, as they actually behave end-to-end at the grid connection -- not a raw DC/cell-level figure from a datasheet if your inverter itself is the real bottleneck.

data.solver_max_charge_kw: Maximum charge power (kW) -- the fastest your system can actually charge, AC-side, as your inverter itself limits it
data.solver_max_discharge_kw: Maximum discharge power (kW) -- the fastest your system can actually discharge, AC-side
data.solver_efficiency_percent: Round-trip efficiency (%, optional) -- combined battery-chemistry + inverter conversion losses. 95% is a reasonable real-world default; NEVER set this to 100% -- a perfectly lossless battery gives the optimizer no real cost to charging and discharging back and forth for no reason, which produces nonsensical plans

solver_grid.title: Solver: Grid Connection (3 of 6)
solver_grid.description: Your real grid connection limits and the live price sensors your electricity retailer or market integration already provides.

data.solver_grid_max_import_kw: Maximum grid import power (kW) -- your real connection/meter limit for buying from the grid
data.solver_grid_max_export_kw: Maximum grid export power (kW) -- your real connection/meter limit for selling to the grid
data.solver_import_price_sensor: Live import (buy) price sensor ($/kWh) -- from your own retailer/market integration
data.solver_export_price_sensor: Live export (sell) price sensor ($/kWh) -- from your own retailer/market integration

solver_sources.title: Solver: Solar & Load Forecasts (4 of 6)
solver_sources.description: Where the Solver gets its forward-looking view of what solar you'll generate and what your house will consume -- point these at your own forecast sensors (Solcast, Open-Meteo, Nimbus's own Power Signals, or anything similar that already exists on your system).

data.solver_solar_forecast_sensor: Solar generation forecast sensor (kW or kWh) -- your existing solar forecast integration
data.solver_load_forecast_sensor: Household load forecast sensor (kW) -- e.g. a Nimbus Power Signal forecasting your own whole-house load

solver_policy.title: Solver: Economic Policy (5 of 6)
solver_policy.description: Small, deliberate friction costs that keep the optimizer's plans sane -- without SOME real cost to cycling the battery, a mathematically "free" battery will charge and discharge pointlessly. The defaults are a safe, sensible starting point; you very rarely need to change them.

data.solver_charge_cost: Charge cost ($/kWh, optional) -- a small real cost/penalty applied to every kWh charged, discourages pointless cycling
data.solver_discharge_cost: Discharge cost ($/kWh, optional) -- a small real cost/penalty applied to every kWh discharged
data.solver_salvage_value: Salvage value ($/kWh, optional) -- how much a kWh still sitting in the battery at the end of the planning horizon is worth keeping vs. selling now; raise this if the optimizer sells the battery down to empty too eagerly

solver_p2p.title: Solver: Peer-to-Peer Bonus (6 of 6, optional)
solver_p2p.description: Only fill this in if you sell energy through a peer-to-peer/community trading scheme (like LocalVolts P2P) that pays a bonus rate for a LIMITED nightly volume, on top of your normal export price. Leave both fields at 0 if this doesn't apply to you.

data.solver_p2p_bonus_price: P2P bonus price ($/kWh, optional) -- the EXTRA amount paid per kWh above your normal export price, for volume within your nightly allotment
data.solver_p2p_bonus_volume_kwh: Nightly P2P bonus volume (kWh, optional) -- how much export per night typically qualifies for the bonus rate before it reverts to normal export price

user.title: Add a load
user.description: Pick the power sensor this load should learn from. Temperature sensors and tuning settings are shared across every load -- set them once via the hub's own "Configure" instead.

user.title: Add a power signal
user.description: Forecast a real power signal directly -- Battery, Solar, Grid, or anything else -- as its own genuine target, using the same forecasting engine as a load. Pick a real MEASURED sensor, never an optimizer's own plan/forecast entity.
